Sunset Hills.name: Sunset Hills
Sunset Hills.basicInfo:
The rolling golden upland of The Southroll — wave after wave of grass-covered hills bathed in perpetual late-afternoon light. Warm soil, low wild herbs, and an air that lulls walkers into unhurried contentment. Every hill crest offers a new unrolling view of gold, and the fireflies begin their disciplined circles as the light deepens toward evening that never quite arrives.

Living Ecology: Glasswing bees work the warmroot flowers while small golden drakes surf the hill lee without flapping. At the lowest hollows, cool springs gather beneath spontaneous shade groves.
Sunset Hills.hiddenInfo:
The perpetual light is sustained low-state mana — the region is the dimension's lifeboat, keeping itself lit for days on residual energy if everything else failed. Hill fox dens concentrate along the northern folds; the foxes neither fear nor welcome visitors but will guide lost walkers home if bribed with sweet grass. Broad Picnic Groves form naturally in the hollows of the hills — circles of shade-trees that appear where no seeds were ever planted, always with a flat stone suitable for laying out food.

Ecological Continuity: The region's residual stability comes from stored low-state mana cycling through living roots and animals. The light does not suspend time, prevent consequences, or force contentment.

Golden Walk.name: Golden Walk
Golden Walk.basicInfo:
The ridge path along the highest crest of The Southroll — a spontaneous footpath the dimension seems to have worn for the pleasure of it, winding hilltop to hilltop through perpetual golden light. Warm-feather birds roost along its length, grass spirits part the growth a stride ahead of walkers, and from the crest's center the whole dimension is faintly visible: a pocket-sized world laid out under endless afternoon.

Living Ecology: The crest path glows rose-gold beneath each footfall, then dims behind it as fireflies close the trail in ordered spirals. Prairie wind arrives on one side and Rift-cool air on the other.
Golden Walk.hiddenInfo:
The Walk's path was never laid or trodden into being; it appeared complete the morning after the Southroll stabilized — the only fully finished feature the dimension ever produced unasked. Walking its full length in a single stretch grants mild, harmless euphoria and (the Chamberlain suspects) slightly improved mana sensitivity. Small spirit dens thread the embankments under the path: grass spirits and foxes share them without tension. Springs surface along the route after heavy warm days, occasionally ringing with firefly dust in the water.

Ecological Continuity: The firefly pattern is a response to airflow and body heat, not a message or judgment. Deviations can reveal ecological disturbance without supplying its cause automatically.

Eastern Clefts.name: Eastern Clefts
Eastern Clefts.basicInfo:
The great fissure system of The Rift March — dark stone gorges twisting into the region's east, deep enough that cold blue light seeps upward from their bottoms at night. The rims echo a heartbeat late. Grassland edges carelessly into stone; the West is the Southroll's warmth, the East is depth, shadow, and something that has not decided whether it is scenery or danger. Cave mouths punctuate the cleft walls — most unplumbed, all unmarked.

Living Ecology: Cold-light fungus paints the deepest walls cobalt while darkroot vines bridge narrow gaps for crawlers and seed. Echo bats make the caverns audible in delayed, layered clicks.
Eastern Clefts.hiddenInfo:
The clefts descend toward the dimensional boundary itself; at a certain depth, visitors feel they are standing at the bottom of the world. Rift crawlers and cave drakes nest in the upper systems, but the deep systems hold unexplored caverns, monster nests of higher-level predators, and ruins of strange geometry that predate the March — materialized fears wear borrowed shapes. At least one fissure mouth reads as a natural dungeon entrance waiting for an occupant. Blue mana ore veins run along the deepest exposed walls, harvested only by the brave or the careless.

Ecological Continuity: The caves support dangerous fauna and future dungeon development but no unestablished culture, population, or ancient empire. Ruins appear only where existing canon or later play gives them a concrete origin.

Rift Overlook.name: Rift Overlook
Rift Overlook.basicInfo:
The grassland rim above the Eastern Clefts — a broad stone knoll where the Rift March's last safe ground meets its first true drop. From the overlook, the whole fissure system is visible: layered ridges sculpting downward into blue-lit dark. Wind rises from below at dusk carrying cold mineral air and, occasionally, a sound not quite echo. A low cairn ring marks the safety line; past it the ground breaks without warning.

Living Ecology: Golden Southroll grass ends in a clean dark rim overlooking the first blue-lit fissures. Cleft foxes den among warm western stones, safely above the rift crawlers' vertical routes.
Rift Overlook.hiddenInfo:
The Chamberlain placed the cairn ring himself after two survey trips, but refuses to survey further without an escort — unusual fear for a being that catalogs monsters without hesitation. Blue-flame wisps rise from the clefts to the overlook on windless nights, circling it twice before sinking back: a behavior he logs but cannot explain. From this point, only the uppermost cave mouths are in sight; the true depths begin where the overlook's map ends and every route beyond is discovery, not documentation.

Ecological Continuity: The Overlook offers observable signs—roost flights, fungal brightness, echo delay—rather than automatic knowledge of what lives in unexplored depths.

Stillwater Shore.name: Stillwater Shore
Stillwater Shore.basicInfo:
The formal coast of The Quiet Shore — the tideline where moon-white sand meets the flat, still air that behaves like unbreathing water. No waves arrive; sound does not travel. Glass crabs drift across the horizon as if skating, and the luminous fish-like entities glide deep beneath the surface of the not-water near the boundary, too far and too strange for study. The most peaceful and solitary place in the Demi-Plane.

Living Ecology: At false midnight the boundary dew gathers into perfect beads, rolls uphill through moon-sand, and disappears into shell beds that feed the western marshes. Glass crabs comb the tideline in silent, parallel rows.
Stillwater Shore.hiddenInfo:
The not-water is the region's unanswered question — the dimension's only undecided coastline. Walking into it presses no resistance; visitors walk back damp in spirit rather than body, as if the not-water touched what they are made of. Objects arrive on this shore with no origin: sealed bottles with no letters, ropes of no ships, lamps of no wreck. The Chamberlain records each, troubled only by his inability to find their source. The pale shore spirits gather on the tide-line at true dusk and face the horizon — the closest thing this dimension has to a ritual no one designed.

Ecological Continuity: The fish-shaped lights beneath the not-water are native boundary grazers following currents of reflected mana. They are living creatures, not trapped souls, omens, or inhabitants of an unseen city.

Moonwhite Strand.name: Moonwhite Strand
Moonwhite Strand.basicInfo:
The long dune line behind the Stillwater Shore — moon-white sand dunes that never shift, backed by pale-flowered salt-grass whose hollow stalks chime once when nothing else disturbs the air. The strand has the dimension's softest footing and the clearest silence; walking it feels like being the first person ever to cross it. Dune foxes den along its folds, and the sand records every track for days without filling them.

Living Ecology: Moonplovers nest among pale-flowered dune-grass, and tide moths suspend pearlescent silk between saltgrass stems. Cedar needles from the Sanctuary occasionally arrive without wind and become the center of new dune gardens.
Moonwhite Strand.hiddenInfo:
The dunes never shift because the strand is a record, not a landscape — the sand holds whatever is written in it, including footprints, small offerings, and half-covered things. Shell crystal forms inside the oldest salt-grass stems. Rarely, an impossible reflection appears in the sand's hollows at dusk: a face, a boat, a figure — usually washed away by morning. Tideline caves open at the strand's western edge on quiet days, tunnels into the duneface that go back several body-lengths and drain into the not-water without flooding.

Ecological Continuity: Pale driftwood is condensed from compatible organic patterns carried by the boundary, then accepted into the Shore's ecology. It does not imply a sea, shipwreck, or outside settlement unless a concrete event establishes one.
